title: optimize
description: Stage output contract: one bounded, measured speed pass, plus the architectural changes it deliberately did NOT make.

measurements.description: what you actually timed, before and after. Required (an empty array is the honest answer for a no-op pass) because an unmeasured speed claim is not a speed claim. MODEL-REPORTED profiling detail — useful for WHY the change was made, but no longer what decides anything: since #520 the engine runs the project adapter's declared benchmark itself, before and after this stage's commit, and keeps the commit only on a measured win (see `benchmark`). Report what you ran, never an estimate.

name.description: what was measured (the benchmark/operation), not the optimization

unit.description: e.g. ms, s, ops/s, MB — state it, or before/after are unreadable

benchmark.description: ENGINE-OWNED verdict (#520) — do NOT author this key: whatever a stage returns here is overwritten by the engine's own before/after run of the project adapter's declared benchmark command, taken at the last-good checkpoint and at this stage's commit. `status` is `verified` (a win beyond the tolerance, commit kept), `no_win` (measured, nothing beyond the tolerance, or a regression — commit reverted), `failed` (the benchmark ran red or printed unreadable output — reverted), `unavailable` (nothing runnable to measure with: no adapter benchmark, a dirty worktree, no anchor — reverted) or `skipped` (the pass committed nothing, so there was nothing to keep or revert).

reverted.description: whether the engine CONFIRMED the stage's commit is off the worktree HEAD — not merely that a reset was attempted. False on a not-kept verdict means the commit may still be on the branch, `revert_unconfirmed` names why, and the stage is failed rather than reported green.

revert_unconfirmed.description: why the engine could not confirm the commit was removed; present only on a not-kept verdict whose revert it could not verify

tolerance.description: the minimum relative improvement this verdict required

metrics.description: one row per metric measured on both sides: name/before/after/unit/lower_is_better/delta_fraction (signed so positive is better)/direction/judged

suggestions.description: architectural changes this stage judged out of its own scope and did NOT apply (a process-pool restructure, a shared-memory layout, a different lock strategy) — so a task never turns into a redesign and the idea is not lost. Optional; omit or return an empty array when there are none. The engine files one as an enhancement issue at finalize only when it carries an explicit `file` disposition, subject to the same per-task cap and title dedupe as a review finding.

description.description: the change itself, one sentence first — its leading line becomes the enhancement issue title

rationale.description: why it would pay off, and what this pass measured that points at it — the issue body

disposition.description: same filing threshold as a review finding's. Choose `file` deliberately, with justification, to open an enhancement issue; `drop` for something a maintainer would not independently prioritize. An absent or unrecognized disposition is surfaced in the completion note, never filed — filing requires explicit `file`.
